title: Alcohol history
candidateBrief: You are a junior doctor on a surgical ward. Morgan Hughes, 51, was admitted yesterday for an elective hernia repair scheduled for tomorrow. The nurses noticed he seems shaky. Take an alcohol history and assess for dependence. You will be asked questions afterwards.

patient.name: Morgan Hughes
patient.setting: Bedside on a surgical ward, curtains drawn.
patient.openingStatement: Morning, doc. The nurse said you wanted a word. I'm fine, just a bit on edge about the operation.
patient.demeanour: Friendly and jokey but becomes defensive and minimises when asked directly about drinking. Hands tremble slightly, a little sweaty and restless.
patient.speechStyle: Casual, jokey, working-class everyday language. Deflects with humour. Honest if the doctor is non-judgemental.

ice.ideas: Thinks the shakes are nerves about surgery.
ice.concerns: Worried the operation will be cancelled and he'll lose more work.
ice.expectations: Wants to get the op done and get home.

freelyShared: Likes 'a few pints after work, like everyone'.
Last drink was the night before admission.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: how much he drinks, type of drink, units per day or week
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: Honestly? Probably six or seven pints of lager a night, more at the weekend. Sometimes a few whiskies too.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: drinking in the morning or an eye-opener
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: Lately I've had a can in the van in the morning to steady my hands.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: what happens when he stops, shakes, sweats, seeing things, fits
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: If I don't have a drink I get the shakes and sweats. Once, a couple of years ago, I had a fit when I tried to stop on my own.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: cutting down, people annoying him about drinking, or guilt
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: The wife's always on at me about it and it does wind me up. I've tried to cut down a few times. I feel bad about it, yeah.

revealOnlyIfAsked.topic: Needing more and letting things slide
revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: needing more to get the same effect, or drinking taking priority
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: I need a lot more than I used to to feel anything. And I've let jobs slide because of it.
keywords: a lot more than i used to

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: impact on work, family, health, driving or the law
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: I got done for drink-driving five years back. Lost my licence for a year.
I get a bit low sometimes, but the drink helps with that.

patient.cue: Look, I know I probably drink more than I should. Is that what this is about?

examFindings.finding: Fine tremor of the outstretched hands. Palmar erythema. No asterixis.
Liver edge palpable 2 cm below the costal margin, smooth, non-tender. Reducible right inguinal hernia.

investigations.result: GGT 210 U/L (high), ALT 64 U/L (high), bilirubin 18 µmol/L, albumin 36 g/L.

postEncounterQuestions.q: Does he meet criteria for alcohol dependence? Justify.
postEncounterQuestions.modelAnswer: Yes: compulsion/cutting down unsuccessfully, tolerance, withdrawal symptoms relieved by drinking (morning drinking), salience over work, continued drinking despite harm.
keyPoints: Loss of control / failed attempts to cut down

postEncounterQuestions.q: What are the immediate risks during this admission and how would you manage them?
postEncounterQuestions.modelAnswer: Risk of alcohol withdrawal including seizures (previous withdrawal fit) and delirium tremens. Start a symptom-triggered or fixed-dose benzodiazepine regimen with a withdrawal scale (e.g. CIWA-Ar), give parenteral thiamine before glucose, monitor observations, inform the surgical and anaesthetic teams, and refer to the alcohol liaison team.

items.text: Introduces self and explains the reason for the conversation
Uses a non-judgemental approach and normalising questions
Quantifies intake (type, amount, pattern) and estimates units
Establishes the time of the last drink
Uses a screening tool (CAGE/AUDIT) or equivalent questions
Asks about dependence features: tolerance, withdrawal, compulsion, salience
items.evidenceHint: more to get the same, shakes when you stop

items.text: Asks about previous withdrawal seizures or DTs
Explores consequences: health, work, relationships, legal, driving
Screens mood and other substance use
Explains withdrawal risk in hospital and offers support/treatment
